summary: Plan a smart crowd-counting and detection application. Keep the scope centered on crowd counting; do not assume the vision model, input data, live-stream support, privacy approach, or deployment target.

questions.question: Which language should the frontend use?

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Typed JavaScript for a maintainable web interface.

questions.rationale: A web interface is a reasonable starting point for configuring and reviewing crowd-counting results.

questions.question: Which frontend framework would you prefer?

options.label: React
options.description: A widely used component-based web framework.

options.label: Other
options.description: Enter a different framework or describe a preference.

questions.question: Which language should the backend API use?

options.label: Python
options.description: A common language for computer-vision integrations.

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Use TypeScript for the API as well as the frontend.

options.label: C# (.NET)
options.description: Use the .NET ecosystem for the API.

questions.rationale: Python is a practical default for integrating a crowd-detection model, but no model or inference approach is assumed.

questions.question: Which backend API framework should be used?

options.label: Azure Functions
options.description: Azure serverless functions for API endpoints.

questions.rationale: Azure Functions is offered as the Azure-native option; enter a custom framework if preferred.

questions.question: Which data or storage services will the application need?

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Do not persist application data or uploaded media.

options.label: Blob Storage
options.description: Store uploaded or retained images, video, or other files.

options.label: Azure SQL
options.description: Store structured application records or detection results.

options.label: PostgreSQL
options.description: Store structured application records or detection results.

options.label: Azure Cache for Redis
options.description: Cache transient or frequently accessed data.

questions.rationale: The input modality, retention needs, and processing pattern have not been specified.

questions.question: Will users sign in to use application features?

options.label: Yes
options.description: Users need authenticated access to application features.

options.label: No
options.description: The application has no user sign-in requirement.

questions.question: Describe the expected crowd-counting workflow and must-have user-facing features. If known, clarify whether input is still images, uploaded video, or live camera streams; do not include sensitive data.
questions.rationale: The requested goal is known, but interaction and input details are not.

questions.question: Describe any known detection/model, throughput, processing, and result-retention requirements. You may say these are undecided; do not provide private images, credentials, or other sensitive data.
questions.rationale: No model, performance target, or retention policy was specified.

questions.question: Describe any privacy, access-control, or data-retention constraints, or indicate that these are undecided.
questions.rationale: Privacy and retention choices should not be inferred for crowd imagery.

questions.question: Where should the application run, if you already know? You can leave deployment undecided.
questions.rationale: No deployment target or environment was specified.
